newsitem.title: USA: Albright laying plans for September trip.
newsitem.headline: Albright laying plans for September trip.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is making plans for a September trip to the Mideast that will focus on speeding Israeli-Palestinian peace talks and also include other stops, her spokesman said Thursday.

"The Secretary of State is going to the Middle East soon. I can assure you of that. The 'when' is linked to the kind of trip she wants to have and the kind of results that we see in the area of security that we are going to be watching in the coming weeks," spokesman James Rubin told reporters.

Rubin said although the trip would focus on Palestinian-Israeli relations, Albright would probably make other stops in the region. "We have broader interests in the region, we have national security interests that go beyond Israel and the Palestinian authority," Rubin said.

Albright said in a speech on Aug. 6 she was prepared to go to the Middle East at the end of August provided progress was made in improving the security situation after a deterioration culminating in a deadly bombing in Jerusalem on July 30.
"It's possible the trip will not be in August but will be in September," Rubin said.

"She is beginning to think a little bit about her schedule -- she is going -- and exactly what she'll do while she's there. And what we're going to do is watch the results over the coming weeks and make a decision on that basis," he said.

U.S. envoy Dennis Ross, who spent the past four days in the region trying to persuade Israelis and Palestinians to resume cooperation on fighting terrorist, is likely to make another trip to the area, Rubin said.
But that mission will be linked to Albright's trip -- her first to the Middle East as secretary of state -- and it is not yet decided whether it would come before or after Albright's visit, he said.
